title: 6.3.3 Lab: Slow it, stop it, count it
description: The table, drag, the stop rule, and a shot counter: you can only shoot from rest.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: Shots work, but the ball never stops and the counter is missing.

steps.title: Drag and stop
steps.instructions: Add `cue.drag` and the stop rule from the sub-build.

steps.title: Shoot only from rest
steps.instructions: Put the release shot inside the stopped test, or add `&& cue.speed === 0`. Add `shots += 1` in the same branch.

steps.title: Count in words
steps.instructions: Show the word Shots and the number on screen.
hints: A counter that climbs without a shot means it is outside the release branch.

requirements.title: The ball slows
requirements.description: Drag is set on the ball. Help: 6.3.1 (Reading: Rolling to a stop)

requirements.title: Stopped is a threshold
requirements.description: Speed under a small number becomes 0 (or a flag). Help: 6.3.1 (Reading: Rolling to a stop)

requirements.title: One shot, one count
requirements.description: The shot count goes up in the release branch, not every frame. Help: 6.3.1 (Reading: Rolling to a stop)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Lab: Slow it, stop it, count it". The task: give the ball drag and a stop threshold, let the player shoot only when it is at rest, and count one shot per release. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: Drag and stop
rubric.description: Both are present, with the stop as a threshold.

rubric.title: Shoot from rest
rubric.description: The release shot is gated by the stopped test.

rubric.title: One count per shot
rubric.description: The counter increments in the release branch.
